name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:mocks → /spec:plan → /spec:run (build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.201.0 — The design contract is code: a host with a UI stack now declares design: {kit, tokens, rules} in its grounding config instead of a single app pointer, and design-contract-check.js is the mechanical presence oracle — it walks the kit directory for intent-named composites, parses the rules file's intent-to-pattern and per-layer naming tables, and reports every gap by kind and remedy. /spec:init locates the three paths and seeds the rules file from a template when absent, running the check as an advisory report rather than a gate; /spec:doctor check 8 runs the same script; /spec:enforce gains the kit-discipline category (folding color/typography/density out of the old forbidden-symbol/structural-pattern split) so a host's kit-backed design rules get a real discovered enforcer alongside everything else. No doctrine prose enforces any of this — the check script and the taxonomy are the only oracles. 7.200.0 — The approval file is not a gate: the per-brief design workbench command and the plan-to-build design stage are deleted along with their frontmatter contract fields, and every plan/run/build/review/status reader of design/approval.json; the three lanes a change can travel (direct, behaviour, structural) are now written once in core.md's Pipeline Entry doctrine. /spec:mocks and genesis are unaffected — they keep writing and reading design/approval.json. 7.199.0 — Mock contract moves to version 3 — design/decisions.json and approval.theme are retired, per-screen approval is recorded by mock-review approve --screen <name> run by the session rather than by a control on the served page, and the mocks driver's client waive now calls the package's waive verb so no script in this repo writes a design document.
